methodological_rigor.justification: In vitro cell biology study using standard methods (transfection, CCK-8, Transwell, flow cytometry, Western blot) with appropriate controls and three biological replicates. Two-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc test applied for proliferation data; normality tested via Q-Q plots. However, critical limitation acknowledged: caspase-3 cleavage status not assessed despite measuring anti-caspase-3, only cleaved-PARP evaluated for apoptosis (line 115). No blinding, no in vivo validation. Knockdown efficiency varies substantially between cell lines (27% vs. 43%), potentially confounding interpretation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: In vitro preclinical study with two ovarian cancer cell lines; maps to LoE 5 per rubric (cell line/mechanistic work). Translational relevance speculative: LINC00473 is already implicated in lung, breast, and hepatocellular carcinoma progression; application to ovarian cancer extends prior work but adds no paradigm shift. Proposed mechanisms (Sox2/YAP1 modulation, CDDP sensitization) plausible but unvalidated in vivo. No patient cohort, no xenograft model, pathway mechanism unproven without functional rescue experiments.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods section is detailed and reproducible: cell sources, culture conditions, transfection protocol with reagent specifics (Lipofectamine 2000), siRNA sequences in Table I, assay endpoints and statistics clearly stated. ARRIVE-adjacent reporting for cell-based work. However, data availability is severely limited: no raw data repository cited, no code/supplementary materials referenced, cell lines sourced from commercial vendors but no statement regarding data sharing. Authors explicitly note no in vivo data due to 'limitations in project duration and funding' (line 123).

novelty_literature.justification: LINC00473 is established as an oncogenic lncRNA in multiple cancers (pancreatic, liver, pituitary, lung, breast, glioma). Present study applies known oncogene to ovarian cancer and validates known pathway partners (Sox2, YAP1). No discovery of novel gene, isoform, or mechanism. Synergy with cisplatin is incremental (similar lncRNA/chemotherapy combinations already reported for HOTAIR/paclitaxel and CCAT1/cisplatin, as cited). Cell line heterogeneity noted (A2780 vs. SK-OV-3 sensitivity) but not mechanistically explained.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is well-organized with clear methodology, results presented logically with time-course data and quantitative fold-changes. Figures referenced appropriately; Discussion contextualizes findings against prior literature and candidly acknowledges limitations (lack of caspase-3 cleavage measurement, absence of in vivo validation, variable knockdown efficiency). Statistical notation (*P<0.05, **P<0.01, ***P<0.001) applied consistently. Minor issue: some redundancy between Abstract results and Results section; one sentence on caspase-3 contains self-correction (lines 115-116).

key_strengths: Rigorous in vitro experimental design with three biological replicates, appropriate statistical methods (two-way ANOVA, Q-Q normality testing), and detailed protocol reproducibility
Comprehensive phenotypic analysis: proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and chemosensitivity assessed in parallel across two cell lines
Transparent acknowledgment of methodological limitations (caspase-3 cleavage not measured, variable knockdown efficiency between lines, lack of in vivo validation)
Clear dose/time-dependent effects demonstrated (siLINC00473+CDDP effects prominent after 48 h); differential cell line sensitivities documented
key_concerns: Incomplete apoptosis characterization: caspase-3 cleavage status not measured despite using caspase-3 antibody—only cleaved-PARP used to infer apoptosis activation, limiting mechanistic clarity
LINC00473 is already established as oncogenic in multiple cancer types; application to ovarian cancer is incremental without novel mechanistic insight or clinical validation
No in vivo validation (xenograft, knockout mouse models) or patient cohort correlation—translational path to clinical application unclear; authors cite project duration/funding limits
Knockdown efficiency is suboptimal and cell-line dependent (27–43% reduction)—lower than comparable lncRNA studies, potentially limiting effect size interpretation
No data availability statement; cell lines sourced commercially but reproducibility of specific knockdown constructs unaddressed; supplementary figures referenced but not provided
Proposed Sox2/YAP1 mechanism lacks functional rescue experiments; no luciferase assays or pathway inhibitor studies to confirm direct regulation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent but incremental in vitro mechanistic study applying known oncogenic lncRNA to new cancer type. Lacks in vivo validation, novel mechanisms, and clinical relevance needed for higher tiers. Appropriate for a specialized cell biology or ovarian cancer journal with major revisions addressing apoptosis assay completeness and in vivo feasibility.
